transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-31
Time: 09:42 PT (scheduled 60m)
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Aaron Cho (Redwood SE), Jared Kim (Redwood CSM), Linda Gomez (Nightingale VP Product), Rahul Menon (Nightingale Head ML Infra), Sofia Li (Nightingale Finance), Tom Brooks (Nightingale SRE)

Summary:
Quarterly health check focusing on recent usage spike in July, cost variances, proposed stability sprint (stage-gate for dedicated capacity), and finance alignment for committed capacity. Agreed to run a short dedicated-pool benchmark and a pilot load test. Security docs link requested and provided.

Topics:
- Usage spike and root-cause hypotheses
- Cost per model and token burn trends
- Latency SLOs and tail latency incidents
- Dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs and stage-gate proposal
- Billing cadence and budget approvals
- Pilot plan and next steps

Shared artifacts referenced:
- Deck: https://redwood.app/decks/nightingale-qbr-aug2026.pdf
- Cost spreadsheet (proto): https://redwood.app/spreadsheets/ng-costs-aug2026.xlsx
- Security pack: https://redwood.app/security/soc2-2025.pdf

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you making time. I'll let Aaron do a quick status on the latency and then we'll jump into cost.
[00:18] Aaron: yeah hi, hey — quick note, we did see the July spike align with the nightly batch retrains, and there was some crazy prefix-kv cache invalidation which bumped token counts, so per-token cost looked up.
[00:35] Rahul: sorry can I interject, that cache invalidation was our rollout of the embedding reindex, we pushed at 02:00 and, um, it accidentally kept cold cache across a subset of requests.
[00:50] Aaron: right, so the fix was to relax the KV TTL in the runtime, that reduced the repeat generation calls, so tokens/day dropped about 27% over the following 48 hours.
[01:06] Linda: okay good, but the finance team still saw a 40% month-over-month jump and they're asking whether this is a one-off or a structural problem — Sofia's here and will speak to that.
[01:20] Sofia: yeah from our view the spike looked correlated with two things, the retrain plus a new product feature that fans out N+3 prompts per user which multiplies tokens. We need to decide if we move that fanout server-side or keep it client-side. If we move it server-side we need predictability in batch windows for budgeting.
[01:48] Maya: good call. For predictability there's three levers: dedicated capacity to cap unit pricing, prefix caching and smarter batching, and model quantization for the heaviest endpoints. We can show modeled savings in a minute.
[02:05] Jared: also worth noting that dedicated capacity gives you predictable throughput but you can still apply autoscale bursts for peak. The stage-gate idea is a commit pilot then go/no-go for a 12-month reserved pool.
[02:22] Tom: quick SRE question — how intrusive is the dedicated deployment? we have strict VPC peering and SSO SAML flows, and any change has to go through our change board.
[02:36] Aaron: for Private/Dedicated we support VPC peering and customer-managed KMS. There is an onboarding checklist — we usually need a short maintenance window. One thing: if you go on-prem, latency is best but ops lift increases.
[02:55] Rahul: can you repeat the KMS line? do you store keys server-side?
[03:03] Aaron: we support both: Redwood-managed KMS and customer KMS via AWS KMS/HSM. For Private we never persist customer plaintext — keys are customer-controlled. I'll share the security pack link after.
[03:20] Linda: security docs are a must, also SOC-2 + ISO are in procurement checklist.
[03:29] Maya: yep, we uploaded the pack earlier: https://redwood.app/security/soc2-2025.pdf and we'll attach the SOC audit summary specifically.
[03:40] [short cross talk]
[04:05] Maya: okay cost modeling — Aaron, do you want to walk the spreadsheet?
[04:11] Aaron: sure. So in the spreadsheet we split by model family: small-dialogue, base-chat, and longcontext-runner. The longcontext-runner is the biggest burn — primarily because of fanout and lack of prefix cache. If you enable prefix/KV caching and a 1.5x batching window, we estimate 35-45% reduction on that route.
[04:36] Sofia: 35-45% sounds great but what about tail latency? we've seen p95 go from 210ms to 650 on some spikes and product can't accept that.
[04:49] Aaron: good point — batching helps amortize cost but increases latency; it's tradeoffs. With dedicated GPUs and continuous batching tuned for your latency distribution, we can keep p95 under 260ms while hitting cost reductions. The config we propose in the deck is a hybrid: dedicated pool for your critical routes and hosted for low-prio noncritical tasks.
[05:12] Rahul: I'm concerned about model rollouts — if we pin a model version to a dedicated pool, does Redwood support automatic fallback to hosted if the pool is saturated?
[05:24] Aaron: yes, smart routing will fallback to compatible model variants in the hosted catalog; we can set policy to prefer dedicated then hosted at degraded throughput. There is also per-route fallback timeout.
[05:37] Linda: timeline question: if we decide to pilot dedicated, how long to stand up?
[05:43] Maya: typical lead is 2-3 weeks for reserved pools with VPC/peering work condensed, but if you opt for a quick canary using hosted dedicated slots it's usually 3-5 days. The full stage-gate (pilot -> commit) is typically 4-6 weeks end-to-end.
[05:58] Tom: change board window may push us to 3 weeks, but that's okay.
[06:06] Aaron: for the pilot load test we recommend a 2-hour scheduled run with synthetic traffic that mirrors your July tail patterns. We'll need SSO and temporary test credentials.
[06:20] Sofia: fine, finance will sign off on pilot cost up to X (TBD) but need exact numbers.
[06:28] Maya: I'll send a per-model cost breakout right after this call that includes the modeled savings from caching and quantization.
[06:35] Rahul: also curious about eval/quality regression monitoring — if we quantize some models, can you hook into our eval suite to detect drift?
[06:45] Aaron: yes, Redwood Optimize can run regression alerts against your prompt set and flag production quality deltas. We can also keep golden-set comparisons during the pilot.
[06:58] Linda: good, that was a procurement ask too.
[07:05] Maya: on SLAs — for Dedicated we offer tighter p99/p95 guarantees and increased retention on logs for audit. Jared, can you summarize the SLA options?
[07:15] Jared: sure. Hosted tier has best-effort latency targets and 99.5 uptime; Dedicated has 99.9 with priority routing and extended log retention. There's an enterprise add-on for on-prem where we can provide N+1 capacity and an SLA extension.
[07:33] Tom: are audit logs exportable to our SIEM?
[07:37] Aaron: yes, audit logs can be shipped to your S3 or our syslog integration, and we support Splunk/Datadog connectors.
[07:47] Sofia: one more finance thing — billing cadence: monthly vs quarterly invoicing, which do customers typically choose?
[07:54] Maya: most enterprise customers with reserved pools pick monthly invoicing and commit tier discounts; some opt quarterly for internal budgeting. We can adapt to your preferred cadence.
[08:05] Rahul: can we get a worked example of month with normal usage vs July spike so procurement can see delta?
[08:12] Maya: yes, that will be in the cost spreadsheet I send.
[08:18] [pause, people shuffling docs]
[08:39] Aaron: quick gotcha to mention — model quantization profiles may need fine-tuning for long-context models; sometimes you get slight degradation on complex question answering. That's why we recommend you include your golden prompts in the eval harness.
[08:58] Linda: understood, we'll pick 100 representative cases.
[09:03] Tom: operationally, for the pilot we need a runbook; who owns the runbook?
[09:09] Jared: Redwood will provide a starter runbook, then we'll collaborate — Nightingale SRE owns the final change control sign-off.
[09:18] Sofia: timing piece — budget committee meets 9/8, if we get cost numbers by 9/3 we can get onto that agenda.
[09:25] Maya: ok target 9/3 for cost numbers. Next, any procurement or legal blockers?
[09:30] Linda: procurement wants to review the SOC summary and encryption details before pilot approval.
[09:36] Maya: will attach the SOC excerpt and an encryption Q&A.
[09:41] Rahul: two quick tech asks — do you expose kernel-level metrics or is it just per-request traces? we need GPU utilization metrics.
[09:50] Aaron: we push GPU utilization and per-instance telemetry into the Redwood console; we can give RBAC-limited dashboard access and an ingestion hook so you can pull metrics to your Prometheus.
[10:05] Tom: perfect.
[10:07] [small crosstalk]
[10:30] Maya: okay time check — wrapping with agreed next steps: we'll share cost sheet, Aaron runs benchmark, Tom provides test access, Sofia confirms budget window. Pilot tentatively scheduled 9/10 for 2 hours.
[10:47] Linda: sounds good. Any last questions?
[10:52] Sofia: no, that's it.
[10:55] Maya: great — thanks all, we'll follow up with calendar invites and artifacts.
[11:03] End of meeting.

Notes on transcript quality: Some speaker attributions may be approximate; system timestamps are from call log. Natural speech artifacts included (ums, fillers) and occasional transcription mistakes (e.g. "prefix-kv" may appear as "prefix q v").

Recap (one-line): Redwood + Nightingale agreed to a pilot for dedicated capacity with a stage-gate to a 12-month reserved pool, action items assigned for cost numbers, benchmark, and pilot access; target dates align to Nightingale's 9/8 budget committee.
